verdict: CoreWeave's revenue more than doubled to $1.36B and the core business scraped an operating profit of $52M — but $311M of net interest expense turned that into a $110M net loss, softened by a $127M tax benefit.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: diluted net loss per share, vs -$1.82 a year ago

kpis.label: Revenue backlog
kpis.note: nearly doubled in the quarter, at Sep 30, 2025

segments.name: AI cloud infrastructure
segments.note: Renting out AI computing power — clusters of GPUs in data centers — to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up 134% YoY as capacity expanded.

opex.name: Technology and infrastructure
opex.note: Running and expanding the platform: data-center operations and the engineering behind the AI cloud; up from $286M a year ago as capacity grew.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Selling the cloud to AI labs, hyperscalers and large enterprises; up from $5M a year ago as the sales effort scaled.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: The back office: finance, legal and company-wide administration; up from $34M a year ago.

follow100Note: Interest and other non-operating costs took $21.15 of every $100 — more than the quarter's entire operating profit. A $127M tax benefit added back $9.28, but the business still lost $8.07 of every $100 it took in.
otherDetail: Net non-operating expense of $289M: interest expense, net was $311M — the cost of borrowing heavily to build data centers — partly offset by $22M of other income, net. There was no fair-value gain or loss this quarter. The tax line was a $127M benefit, not a bill.
footerNote: Gross profit = revenue less cost of revenue. The $110M net loss is drawn as 'Covered by cash on hand'.

takeaways.title: Revenue more than doubled, again
takeaways.text: Revenue hit $1,365M, up from $584M a year ago, and the revenue backlog — work customers have committed to — almost doubled in one quarter to more than $55B.

takeaways.title: An operating profit, swallowed by interest
takeaways.text: The core business earned $52M of operating income, but interest expense, net of $311M on the debt used to build data centers pushed the quarter to a $237M pre-tax loss. A $127M tax benefit cut the final net loss to $110M.

takeaways.title: Cash earnings look very different
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA — a non-GAAP cash-earnings view that strips out interest, taxes and non-cash costs — was $838M, a 61% margin, and adjusted operating income was $217M versus $52M on a GAAP basis.

oneTimers: The tax line was a $127M benefit, not a bill — without it, the net loss would have been $237M instead of $110M.
Unlike a year ago, there was no fair-value adjustment this quarter; Q3 2024's results carried a $341M fair-value loss, which is a big reason the year-ago net loss was $360M.
